title: Health check roadmap & KPI decomposition
body:
Purpose: This working doc breaks a compact set of customer-facing signals into measurable definitions, ownership, alert thresholds and a short remediation playbook. Aim is a single-page signal map for QBR slides and the renewal health checklist. This is intentionally concise and iterative — comments welcomed.

Scope: metrics covered here: latency (multiple flavors), uptime (service and request success), cost-per-token (effective unit economics), and cache hit rate (prefix/KV). Notes include measurement windows, sampling, and how to present near-term actions in a QBR.

1) Latency — decompose and measure
- Definitions:
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token): time from request arrival at edge to the first token emitted to customer; sensitive to cold starts and first-token kernel path.
  - P50 generation latency: median time to full response completion for generation requests (end-to-end).
  - P95 / P99 tail latency: 95th and 99th percentile completion latencies — used for SLA and customer experience story.
  - Per-token latency: average time spent computing each subsequent token (useful when comparing batching/kv-cache effects).
- Measurement window: rolling 7-day for operational dashboards; 90-day for trend and QBR narrative.
- Sampling & aggregation: calculate percentiles from request-level completion times. For large customers, compute per-customer percentiles before aggregating to avoid heavy skew from bursty power users.
- Presentation guidance for QBR: show 7-day p95 vs baseline, 90-day trend sparkline, and a short note on significant deviations (>30% increase vs baseline).
- Typical targets (example): 
  - TTFT target: < 120 ms for hosted small models, < 200 ms for private with on-prem networking.
  - P95 completion: < 600 ms for short prompts; < 2s for long-context batched workloads.
- Owner & escalation: customer-success owns communication; SRE/serving-runtime owns investigation.

Remediation playbook (latency):
- If p95 increases by >25% week-over-week: 1) Check routing fallback events (traffic spilled to cheaper/compatible model) 2) Inspect KV-cache hit rate and prefix miss patterns 3) Verify autoscaler and GPU utilization for Dedicated customers 4) If private: check network egress/ingress metrics and local node health.

2) Uptime & success rate
- Definitions:
  - Service uptime: % of time the API gateway accepted requests and returned a 2xx/3xx/4xx within SLA window (measured at the edge).
  - Request success rate (invocation success): ratio of requests that succeeded (2xx) vs all started requests (including 5xx/timeout).
  - Healthy instance fraction: for Dedicated/Private, percent of serving instances reporting healthy KV and GPU checks.
- Measurement windows: 30-day rolling and 365-day for contractual SLAs.
- SLO vs SLA: SLO set for internal ops (e.g., 99.9% monthly), SLA is contractual (e.g., 99.5%). Use separate metrics in QBR; do not conflate.
- Presentation guidance: show monthly uptime with incident callouts and mitigation (what caused the delta, what fixed it).

Remediation playbook (uptime):
- If monthly uptime drops below SLO by >0.1%: 1) Triage incident timeline in first 1 hour, 2) Run health-check playbook: re-route traffic, enable fallback model, notify CS + customer, 3) Prepare postmortem draft within 72 hours.

3) Cost per token (effective unit cost)
- Definition: total serving cost attributable to customer / billed tokens. Serving cost should include GPU-minutes, network egress (if billable), and caching amortization. For Hosted, include per-token infra allocations; for Dedicated, use committed capacity amortization + burst incremental cost.
- Calculation method (recommended):
  - Period cost = infra spend assigned to customer (or proportional share for shared pools) + caching infra amortization + licensing (if any)
  - Effective cost-per-token = Period cost / tokens_generated (include prompt + completion tokens)
- Presentation guidance: show current period vs baseline, and a sensitivity table for changes in batch size, model variant (float16 vs quantized), and cache hit improvements.
- Targets & narratives: highlight actions that move cost-per-token without degrading quality: batching config changes, quantization profile, cache warmers.

Remediation playbook (cost):
- If cost-per-token increases >15% month-over-month: 1) Run model-variant drift check (did customer switch to larger model?), 2) Review batching config and average tokens-per-request, 3) Propose immediate mitigations: enable small-model fallback for low-risk endpoints, increase cache TTL for stable prefixes, or apply recommended quantization profile.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix & KV cache)
- Definitions:
  - Prefix cache hit rate: percent of requests where a cached prefix produced a full/partial answer without full model recompute.
  - KV cache efficiency: percent of token-generation steps served from KV cache vs cold attention recompute.
- Measurement: track both per-request (did we use cached prefix?) and per-token (how many token-ops avoided). Report both numbers for richer storytelling.
- Typical targets: hosted product benchmark: prefix hit >= 35% for assistant-style workloads; KV token savings >= 45% for conversational workloads with repeated context. Private/dedicated baselines can be lower depending on customer prompt patterns.

Remediation playbook (cache):
- If prefix hit < target: 1) Examine prompt variability (are callers including unique request ids or timestamps?), 2) Propose prompt-normalization guidance to customers, 3) Suggest client-side prefixing best-practices and warming.

5) KPI table (compact) — use this for QBR slide + renewal checklist
- Columns: signal | target | alert threshold | primary owner | immediate action | QBR talking point
- Example rows (as CSV-like lines for copy):
  - "TTFT (first-token) | <150 ms | >250 ms sustained 7d | Eng-SRE | Run cold-start audit, enable warm-pool | \"Stable first-token latency; warmed fleet reduces cold starts\""
  - "P95 completion | <1s (short prompts) | >1.5s 7d | Serving-runtime | Check routing, autoscale, KV-miss spikes | \"P95 improved after canary\""
  - "Monthly uptime | >=99.9% SLO | <99.5% month | Eng-SRE/CS | Incident triage + workaround | \"Single region incident mitigated by fallback\""
  - "Cost-per-token | baseline +/-(10%) | +15% MoM | CS + Optimize | Propose batching/quantize plan | \"Opportunity: 18% saving via quantization\""
  - "Prefix cache hit | >=35% | <25% 14d | CS + Serving-runtime | Prompt normalization + cache warming | \"Cache savings reduced by recent client change\""

6) Narrative & QBR framing notes
- For QBR, lead with 3 signals: availability (uptime), end-user latency (p95), and unit economics (cost-per-token) — then surface cache as an efficiency lever.
- Provide: current vs baseline numbers, incident highlights (if any), and a single prioritized recommendation with estimated impact (e.g., \"enable small-model fallback: estimated -12% cost / +0.05s p95\").
- Use qualitative customer feedback (support tickets, CS notes) to correlate metric shifts with product changes.

7) Measurement gotchas & common pitfalls
- Aggregation bias: do not report fleet-level median for a single large customer; compute per-customer metrics first.
- Timezones and billing windows: ensure cost windows align with billing period used in QBR.
- Cache definitions differ across products — always annotate whether prefix vs KV-token savings are shown.

8) Next steps & checklist before QBR
- Validate 7-day and 90-day windows for each metric (eng owners sign off).
- Build 1 slide: signal map + KPI table + one prioritized action.
- Run customer-specific simulation for proposed fix (e.g., simulate batching changes) and capture estimated cost/latency delta.
- CS owner to prepare 2–3 talking points mapping metrics to customer impact.

Feedback & open questions (notes to self):
- Should we include example alert thresholds that map to dollar impact? (e.g., +$X/day when cache drops by Y) — would help economic framing.
- Do we want to standardize a single measurement script for per-customer percentiles to avoid aggregation mistakes?

Document status: working draft; will iterate with Eng-SRE and Optimize to lock final numbers and thresholds.

Appendix: quick formulas
- Request success rate = successful_requests / total_requests * 100
- Effective cost-per-token = allocated_infra_cost_period / tokens_generated_period
- Prefix hit rate = requests_using_cached_prefix / total_requests * 100

End of doc.
